root.label: Bit manipulation
root.note: The bit header counts and rotates by exact type width; shifts and promotion are where the surprises live.

children.label: Counting and rotating
children.note: These functions take unsigned types only and use the width of the exact type, with no promotion to int.

children.label: popcount
children.note: Counts the set bits of an unsigned integer.

children.label: countl_zero, countr_zero
children.note: Count leading or trailing zeros in the width of the argument type; countl_zero(uint8_t{1}) is 7.

children.label: rotl and rotr
children.note: Rotate within the type width; any count is allowed and a negative count reverses direction.

children.label: Power-of-two helpers
children.note: has_single_bit, bit_width, bit_floor and bit_ceil describe a value's relation to powers of two.

children.label: has_single_bit
children.note: True only for powers of two, so false for zero.

children.label: bit_floor, bit_width
children.note: bit_floor(0) is 0, bit_width(0) is 0, and bit_floor(37u) is 32.

children.label: bit_ceil precondition
children.note: Undefined if the result does not fit the type; constant evaluation rejects it.

children.label: Reinterpreting bytes
children.note: bit_cast, byteswap and endian handle object representation without aliasing violations.

children.label: bit_cast
children.note: Needs equal sizes and trivially copyable types; constexpr unless pointers, unions or references are involved.

children.label: byteswap (C++23)
children.note: Reverses the bytes of any integer type and knows nothing about the host order.

children.label: std::endian
children.note: little, big and native describe byte order; native may equal neither on a mixed-endian platform.

children.label: Shift counts
children.note: The right operand has to be within range for both shift directions.

children.label: Count out of range
children.note: A negative count or one at least the promoted width is undefined, for signed and unsigned alike.

children.label: Result type
children.note: The result has the promoted type of the left operand; the count's type does not matter.

children.label: Mask pitfall
children.note: (1u << n) - 1 fails at n equal to the width; guard the edge cases.

children.label: Signedness and promotion
children.note: Narrow operands become int before shifts and bitwise operators, and C++20 tightened signed shifts.

children.label: Right shift, C++20
children.note: Negative values shift arithmetically, rounding toward negative infinity, so -7 >> 1 is -4.

children.label: Left shift, C++20
children.note: Signed left shift is modular and two's complement, so -1 << 3 is -8.

children.label: Promotion trap
children.note: ~uint8_t{15} is the int -16, and uint8_t{0x80} << 24 is a negative int.

children.label: Two's complement
children.note: C++20 requires signed integers to use two's complement.

children.label: Bytes and bit-fields
children.note: Use std::byte for raw memory and be wary of bit-fields in external formats.

children.label: std::byte
children.note: Supports bitwise operators and shifts, no arithmetic; convert with std::to_integer.

children.label: Bit-field layout
children.note: Allocation order and straddling are implementation-defined, so use masks for wire formats.
